review: M3-C r3 law and contract soundness

requiredFindings.problem: The opensip.json digest join only compares a carrier read by the walk. It does not require the operationally captured carrier to have a matching row at sealing or specify agreement with an absent-carrier observation, so disappearance before the walk escapes the stated join.
evidence: M3-B item 2 makes the project carrier optional: absent is no layer. Item 5 records its exact digest when present.
PROPOSAL.md:110 keeps B1's carrier bytes outside the capture session; the session's leftover-capture rule at :117 cannot account for this operational capture.

Counterexample: X2 captures/rechecks an opensip.json selecting policy/budget under the fence; after handoff the file is removed before root enumeration. The walk reads no carrier, so :103's digest comparison does not run, while B1's resolved configuration remains available for binding.
C1-T25 at :132 specifies a rewrite control, not present-to-absent or absent-to-present. X2's admission recheck does not specify a later C1 sealing join.
requiredFindings.fix: Retain observed carrier presence with an optional digest, with no raw-byte handoff or MarkerObservation change. At sealing require a present carrier to have exactly one inventory row of the captured digest and require stable absence for the absent case. Refuse presence changes, content changes or exclusion of a required present carrier as SnapshotCarrierChanged, without retry; state ignorePaths interaction. Add disappearance, creation and stable-absence controls.

requiredFindings.problem: Logical protocol counts are applied during decoding before activation and final package admission establish the actual dependency-set population. Inactive or subsequently rejected candidates can therefore trigger a whole-import DependencySetBound although the admitted set is within every protocol bound.
evidence: native_evidence_model.v2.py:1832-1845 iterates activated packages, skips path packages and selects supplied rows; :1870-1883 builds the admitted descriptor and fileCount/totalBytes from that population.

PROPOSAL.md:515-518 orders materialization of every supplied package before Cargo computes activation and before activated-set admission, while :490 stops decoding and refuses on a protocol-counter crossing.

An in-profile activated package containing one byte plus an in-profile inactive supplied package containing 8 GiB yields 8 GiB+1 over supplied candidates but only one byte in the admitted set. arithmetic_checks.json records this without constructing any archive.

An archive rejected by a late gzip-trailer or tar-profile check has no admitted package under :500-506. Its provisional content must not remain in final admitted-set totals or replace the missing/undecodable disposition with an unsupported set overflow.
requiredFindings.fix: Keep provisional acquisition/decoder accounting separate from protocol totals. Commit logical counts only for successfully admitted packages in the activated, non-path set population, and enforce protocol bounds before publishing its descriptor/transport. Any early protocol refusal must prove overflow of that population. Give any independent pre-activation resource cap its own owner, quantity and disposition. Add inactive in-profile excess and late outside-profile rejection controls.

nonBlockingObservations.observation: The claimed 2^33-byte allowance for 8 GiB plus metadata has zero room beyond 8 GiB, and WorkCost.bytes measures charged storage rather than only payload. Existing bounded-reader growth and native metadata/capture buffers require separate pricing. This is not a proof that a streaming C1 implementation must exhaust the proposed cap.
evidence: At product 30c5db1, work_reader.rs:26-54,158-172 charges cumulative buffer growth; a 4 MiB bounded read has 12578817 growth bytes.
filesystem/path_binding.rs:117-126 and descriptor_acl_capture.rs:111-124 charge metadata and capture storage independently.
arithmetic_checks.json records both the equal-cap arithmetic and the reader-growth illustration; no product reader ran.
nonBlockingObservations.suggestion: Specify the snapshot owner's cost recipe and derive its cap from charged buffers, copies and metadata. Extend byte evidence alongside the object/edge census and C1-T20; do not use the payload bound as the complete ledger-cost derivation.

nonBlockingObservations.observation: D3's full-sized stored-block ratio is not universal DEFLATE behavior; establish its producer margin from R6's pinned compressor/configuration. The 16386-byte L example violates D2 while retaining the same 16896 padded bytes, so it does not by itself cross D1. The old unqualified decompression-bound set refusal also needs updating. No legitimate Cargo D3 counterexample was established.
evidence: RFC 1951 sections 2 and 3.2.4 permit arbitrary block sizes and define stored-block LEN/NLEN; blocks need not contain 65535 bytes.
arithmetic_checks.json computes identical block-padded lengths for payloads of 16385 and 16386 bytes.
nonBlockingObservations.suggestion: Include the pinned compressor and streaming-prefix margin in C3a/R6 evidence, give D1 a distinct boundary-crossing control, and qualify C3-T6 so a decoder breach keeps its archive-profile disposition.

nonBlockingObservations.observation: The capture origin must be operational side metadata, not an added member of a closed source-inventory Blob. Older project-byte/read-site wording is broader than the newly defined source-only boundary.
nonBlockingObservations.suggestion: Keep identity inventory rows exactly {path,sha256,bytes}; retain/test origin separately. Narrow the old read prohibition and read-site control to source reads so permitted X2/VCS operational reads and rechecks remain explicit.
